architecturalFinding.verdict: C — multiple variants of ONE shared template pattern, not five isolated mistakes
evidence: every affected chapter carries the same inline <style> block shape: one pedagogical role-highlight rule on line 15 (or ~33), then identical #vocab-grid gender-tag, .vword-de .art, .btn-primary, .mic-btn, .audio-play-btn, .audio-track-fill overrides in the same order

the pedagogical rule names chapter-specific teaching classes (.r-praesens, .r-simul, .r-addition, .r-schwach, .r-kohaerenz, .r-indem, .r-anstatt …) in the SAME .r-* namespace the engine uses for canonical grammar roles
collisions happen when a chapter-specific list happens to include a name that is also canonical (r-verb, r-time, r-negation, r-genitiv, r-modalverb, r-purpose, r-temporal, r-place)
the benign majority (36 restatements, 35 of them .r-genitiv) shows the same template being used correctly — it restates the canonical token rather than replacing it
architecturalFinding.intent: the local rules were written to highlight a chapter’s teaching focus (teal + weight), not to recolour grammar roles

fixOptions.shape: Rename chapter-local pedagogical classes out of the r-* namespace (e.g. .kw-focus-verb or .t-praesens)
fixOptions.blastRadius: edits every colliding chapter HTML plus any data/JS that emits those class names
fixOptions.maintainability: best long-term — makes collision structurally impossible; the namespace becomes single-authority
fixOptions.riskToChapterStyling: medium: the class must be renamed in BOTH the <style> and wherever the token role is authored, or the highlight silently disappears
fixOptions.scope: per-chapter edits, no shared template exists to change

fixOptions.shape: Scope the local rule under a chapter container (e.g. .chapter-c1-01 .r-verb)
fixOptions.maintainability: poor — raises specificity to 0,2,0 and makes the canonical rule permanently unreachable in that chapter; entrenches the defect

fixOptions.shape: Drop the canonical name from the local selector list, keeping only the genuinely chapter-specific classes
fixOptions.blastRadius: one selector edit per collision; 8 distinct chapters for the colour-changing cases
fixOptions.maintainability: good, minimal diff, no renaming of authored data
fixOptions.riskToChapterStyling: low — the chapter-specific classes keep their highlight; only the canonical role reverts to its grammar colour
fixOptions.scope: per-chapter, but the smallest correct change

fixOptions.shape: Move role colours behind a higher-specificity canonical rule in chapter.css (e.g. .de.r-verb) or add a linting rule that fails the build on r-* collisions
fixOptions.blastRadius: one shared file (chapter.css) or one lint rule
fixOptions.maintainability: strongest systemic guard; a lint rule prevents recurrence, which options 1-3 do not
fixOptions.riskToChapterStyling: raising canonical specificity would silently kill legitimate local overrides that are currently intentional (e.g. the .r-es dotted-underline treatment in b2-05)
fixOptions.scope: shared — plus a lint rule; does not by itself repair the 8 chapters
